Pim Pam is a collection of activities to play with one or two switches. It is designed for learning to use switches: every press has a clear visual and sound response. A small “pim” makes a big “pam”.
little films, which move on one sequence with each press. The activities are grouped in folders, and in «Personal activities» new ones can be made with your own photos, videos and sounds.

Switches can come in as keys, as mouse buttons or game controller buttons, and the screen can also be touched. In «Settings» you can adjust one- or two-switch mode, the timing and look of the scanning, the sound, the scenery and the signal that shows when you can press again. Settings can be saved for each user.

Pim Pam works inside the browser and can be used online for free. It can also be installed as an app with the “Install” button on the home page: all the activities are downloaded and it works offline. The sounds and pictures are inside the application itself: no personal data is asked for and whatever is saved stays on this device.
Pim Pam was created at the Unit of Augmentative Communication Techniques (UTAC), using artificial intelligence tools.

UTAC is a team of the University of Barcelona and the Bosch i Gimpera Foundation. It carries out its work through two services of the Government of Catalonia: UTAC Educació, of the Department of Education and Vocational Training, and UTAC Sírius, of the Department of Social Rights and Inclusion.

Most of the sound effects, nature ambiences and animal sounds, and some instruments (kalimba, udu, vibraphone, drum and guitar), were generated with ElevenLabs. They are not real recordings: they have been trimmed, levelled and, some of them, looped. The drawings, animations and music of the activities are generated by the application’s code, and the videos of the journeys are recordings of those same scenes. The videos of the little films were generated with Seedance 2.5, by ByteDance. The pictures and sounds of the activities that began with ChatGPT are those of the files that tool delivered.

A descent through the sea, from the surface to the bottom of the abyss, among creatures of glass, silk and light. With each press the camera travels to the next creatures: a fleet of blue sails, moon jellyfish, a silver shoal, Venus’s girdles, salps, sea angels, a siphonophore, the vampire squid, pyrosomes, glass sponges, dumbo octopuses… Each scene has its own movement, colours and music played on real acoustic instruments. When it ends, the scene stops and darkens until the next press. After the twentieth scene, the camera rises back to the surface.

A descent through the American rainforest, from the dawn sky to the riverbed at night. With each press the camera travels to the next animals: macaws, toucans, hummingbirds, a sloth, morpho butterflies, tamarins, the red-eyed tree frog, poison dart frogs, leafcutter ants, glowing mushrooms, fireflies, capybaras, the giant water lily, the pink river dolphin, stingrays and the arapaima. Each scene has its own movement, light and music played on real acoustic instruments with rainforest sounds. When it ends, the scene stops and darkens until the next press. After the twentieth scene, the camera rises back up to the sky.

A day in the East African savanna, made of cut paper like a diorama: from dawn on Kilimanjaro to the starry night. With each press the camera travels to the next animals: flamingos, crowned cranes, giraffes, elephants, zebras, impalas, warthogs, wildebeest crossing the river, hippos, kingfishers, rhinos, inside a termite mound, mongooses, weavers, cheetahs, lions at sunset, the baobab with bats, the dung beetle and the aardvark. Each scene has its own movement, its time of day and its own music of kalimba, hand drum and shaker, with the sounds of the savanna. When it ends, the scene stops and darkens until the next press. After the twentieth scene, the camera rises back up to the starry sky, ready for another dawn.

A voyage across the world’s oceans, from the Arctic to the Southern Ocean. With each press the camera travels through the water to a great sea animal that swims in, makes its most spectacular move and leaves: narwhals in the ice, belugas, the bowhead whale breaking the ice, the basking shark, humpbacks and their bubble net, a school of tuna, sperm whales sleeping upright, the fin whale, the ocean sunfish, dolphins at the bow of a sailing boat, the humpback’s leap, hammerhead sharks, the oarfish, spinner dolphins, the whale shark, manta rays, the dugong, the right whale with her calf, orcas and the blue whale. Each scene has its own light, sounds and music on acoustic instruments. When it ends, the scene stops and darkens until the next press. After the twentieth scene, the camera rises with the blue whale to the surface, at sunset.

A journey through time across the layers of rock: from the Ice Age to the first dinosaurs. With each press the camera goes down through the rock to a fossil that wakes up and comes to life: mammoths, smilodons, the woolly rhinoceros and the giant deer, the megatherium, tyrannosaurs, triceratops, the ankylosaurus, the Pyrenean abditosaurus, the velociraptor, the citipati on its nest, parasaurolophus, the pteranodon and the plesiosaur, the spinosaurus, the yutyrannus, iguanodons, the archaeopteryx, the stegosaurus, the brachiosaurus and the diplodocus, the ichthyosaurs and the eoraptor. Each scene is a little story with its own light, sounds and music on acoustic instruments. When it ends, the scene stops and darkens until the next press. After the twentieth scene, the camera rises back to today’s garden, where a robin is singing.

Each press moves the day on in a paper village: dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, sunset, evening, night and small hours. At each moment something different happens, and each day is different from the one before.

A night sky over a landscape. Each press lights up a big star, joins it to the previous one with a thread of light and makes something happen in the landscape. At the last one, the stars draw a figure that fills with colour, crosses the sky and breaks up into shooting stars.

A town festival square sewn in felt. Each press sends a balloon up to the sky, and each balloon sings one note of the round’s song. At the last one, when the sky is full, all the balloons rise together while the whole song plays. The balloons never pop. Each round changes the square, the time of day, the colours and shapes of the balloons and the song.

A night sea engraved in wood. The lighthouse beam sweeps slowly over the water. If you press when the light touches a boat, the boat lights its lanterns and the lighthouse guides it to port, where a little band welcomes it. If you press at another moment, the water shines and the light carries on. Every three boats the night changes. In the settings you choose the speed of the light, how long there is to get it right and how many boats there are.

A little painted theatre and a cartoon magician. Each press is a trick that goes wrong in a different way: the never-ending handkerchief, the squirting flower, the wand that ties itself in a knot, the feathered hat, the jumping cards and the tablecloth. Whatever falls stays on the stage. At the last one, the magician goes into the magic wardrobe, comes out of a giant hat, all the mess disappears and he takes a bow. Each round changes the order of the tricks and the colours of the theatre.

A house on a comic-book street. After a while someone knocks at the door: the door shakes and light shows underneath. When you press, the door opens and out comes a visitor who does something funny: the giant who hardly fits, the stuck big-head, the never-ending band, the snowman, the astronaut, the cook and the dancer. If you press before they knock, nothing happens. At the last visit, everyone dances in the street. In the settings you choose how long to wait before they knock and whether the visitor leaves when nobody opens.

A fair of printed tin toys. Above the stall there are three big light bulbs that light up one by one with three rising notes: when the third one lights up, it is time to press. Then comes the launch: the Catalan skittles player, the human cannonball, the wind-up rocket, the strongman who rings the bell or the horse race, and each launch ends with a different surprise and a medal hung on the stall. If you press too early nothing happens. After 3, 5 or 7 launches the ride ends and the stall turns to the next one. Five rides with four lights of the day: twenty rounds.

A 1960s picture book painted in gouache. A waiter holds a tray with one hand. With each press the kitchen door opens and something flies out and lands on the pile: plates, a cup, a cake, a teapot, a watermelon or a fruit platter. The pile wobbles more and more and the waiter balances harder and harder. At the last one a jelly arrives, the waiter is very proud of it and a little mishap (a sneeze, a banana skin or the hiccups) makes everything fall in slow motion: nothing breaks, everything lands somewhere safe and the jelly ends up on his head. Each round changes the order, the character, the place and the mishap.

A party stage in the dark, with empty chairs. Each press wakes up a section of the orchestra, which joins the same piece with recorded instruments; at the last one, they all play together. Each round changes the piece, the place and the order.

A trencadís square on the day of the town festival. The first press forms the pinya with the baixos and each of the next ones raises a tier: the segons, the terços, the quarts, the dosos, the aixecador and the enxaneta (seven presses); something different happens in the square at each tier. At the last one, the enxaneta raises a hand, the square celebrates and the castell comes down slowly. A real castell tune plays, with gralles and drum, recorded at a diada: each press plays the next part, and the raised hand comes with the end of the gralles and the applause. Each round changes the castell, the square, the time of day and the team colour (or the team always wears the shirt colour chosen in the settings).

A landscape painted in brushstrokes. While you hold the switch down the wind blows, and the longer you hold, the stronger it gets: the trees bend, the grass ripples and petals, leaves or washing fly.
